entries.clue: Not abstract material (8)

blocks.note: the adjective sense: real, tangible, existing in physical form
the noun sense: the building material of cement, sand and gravel

annotation.surface: A remark about art or fabric that is anything but conceptual.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase, 'material that is not abstract', but they split into an adjective and a noun that share a spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: Concrete things are real and physical, the opposite of abstract ones, and the same word names the grey building material.

entries.clue: See 24
Cleaner, someone despondent keeping quiet (6)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so MOPER holds P within

blocks.note: moper = someone who mopes, first two letters

annotation.surface: A gloomy cleaner who says nothing while working.
annotation.walkthrough: The quiet P goes into MOPER right beside its own P, so the answer has a doubled P.
annotation.definitionFit: A mopper cleans floors with a mop, a cleaner named by his tool.

entries.clue: Disappointment making one deflated (3,4)

blocks.note: the verb sense: letting a tyre down deflates it, and failing a person deflates them too

annotation.surface: Being disappointed leaves you feeling flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deflated' works both ways: a person let down and a tyre let down are both deflated.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain dictionary uses: the noun for an anticlimax, and the phrasal verb for releasing air or failing someone.

entries.clue: Status of e.g. priest in trouble (8)

indicatorNotes.in trouble: letters in trouble are in disorder

blocks.note: the abbreviation's letters are used as they stand

annotation.surface: A cleric in a scandal loses his standing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'e.g.' looks like mere punctuation leading to an example, but its letters EG are part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prestige is high standing in others' eyes, a kind of status.

entries.clue: A clan out to catch cunning one disregarding convention? (10)

indicatorNotes.out: letters out of order are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to catch: the rearranged clan catches ARCH I and holds it inside

blocks.note: A CLAN rearranged as ANCAL; its first two letters
the rest of ANCAL, closing around ARCH I

annotation.surface: A rebellious clan goes out to capture a crafty rule-breaker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cunning one disregarding convention' reads as one person, but the definition is only the last two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Anarchical behaviour ignores rules and conventions; the question mark flags the loose fit.

entries.clue: Soldiers, excellent, in danger (6)

annotation.surface: Brilliant soldiers caught in a perilous situation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container instruction here: it only links the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a menace is a threat, something that puts you in danger.

entries.clue: Sleepy mum in bed – very big, with little energy (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places mum physically inside the bed, so MA sits within COT

annotation.surface: An exhausted, heavily pregnant mother lying in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little energy' is just the abbreviation E, not a hint about tiredness.
annotation.definitionFit: Comatose is used loosely for extremely drowsy or sluggish, an exaggerated sleepiness.

entries.clue: Outdoor official showing wrath by river (6)

annotation.surface: A park warden losing his temper beside a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' means beside, so either order is allowed; the river goes first.
annotation.definitionFit: A ranger is an official who patrols parkland or forest, working outdoors.

entries.clue: Polluted water in sort of current coming to one ditch (4,4)

blocks.note: a drain is a ditch for water

annotation.surface: Dirty water running along in a stream into a ditch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests a water flow, but it is electrical. The answer continues at 24 across.
annotation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall polluted by sulphur and nitrogen emissions.

entries.clue: Fantastic speed, fantastic train? One only moves at a few mph (10)

annotation.definition: One only moves at a few mph

indicatorNotes.Fantastic: fantastic = wildly altered, so SPEED is rearranged

annotation.surface: An excited advert for a superfast train, undercut by a remark about slowness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all velocity, yet the answer is the slowest traveller of all.
annotation.definitionFit: A pedestrian walks, at around three or four miles an hour.

entries.clue: Problem with shifting Easter (6)

indicatorNotes.shifting: the letters of EASTER shift position

annotation.surface: The perennial difficulty that Easter falls on a different date each year.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Easter is a movable feast, which makes 'shifting' feel like description rather than instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A teaser is short for brain-teaser, a puzzle set to test you, so a synonym for a problem.

entries.clue: Smashing person at crazy party to perform as vocalist outside (10)

indicatorNotes.outside: the singing stands outside, wrapped around the partygoer, so SING encloses HATTER

blocks.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the mad tea party in Alice in Wonderland
the rest of SING, closing around HATTER

annotation.surface: A terrific guest at a wild party who bursts into song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise for the person, and it is the definition in its sense of breaking things apart.
annotation.definitionFit: Smashing and shattering both mean breaking into pieces, and both are also slang for tremendous.

entries.clue: Number in course of day becoming burdened (8)

indicatorNotes.in course of: something in the course of a day happens within it, so EIGHT sits within WED

blocks.note: rest of WED, closing around EIGHT

annotation.surface: Over the day a count grows until it becomes a load.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Day' has to be abbreviated: WED is the calendar short form of Wednesday.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something weighted has had weight put on it, as a burdened thing carries a load.

entries.clue: False debater taken to task (7)

indicatorNotes.False: a false version of DEBATER is its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A dishonest debater gets reprimanded.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a tidy morality tale, and the fodder is a single word that uses every letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to berate is to scold angrily, and 'taken to task' is the idiom for being reprimanded.

entries.clue: Dirtier air there blown around (8)

indicatorNotes.blown around: the letters are blown around into a new order

annotation.surface: Polluted air swirling about somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blown' suits the air perfectly, which disguises it as an indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthier means more soiled with earth, hence dirtier; it also carries the cruder sense of dirty.

entries.clue: Bird gets something to eat by pile of hay? (7)

blocks.note: a pea is something to eat
a cock (haycock) is a small conical pile of hay

annotation.surface: A bird finds food beside a haystack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pile of hay' leads to the farming word cock, a small heap of hay in a field, not to rooster.
annotation.definitionFit: A peacock is a large bird famous for its tail, a definition by example.

entries.clue: Vehicles I love appearing in hit lists (8)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: to appear in something is to show up inside it, so I O shows up inside CHARTS

annotation.surface: A pop fan boasting about how much they love cars that reach the charts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit lists' sounds sinister, but it means the pop charts.
annotation.definitionFit: Chariots are horse-drawn vehicles, a definition by example.

entries.clue: Changes in advertisements – only recently being introduced (7)

indicatorNotes.being introduced: to introduce something is to bring it in, so JUST is brought into ADS

blocks.note: first two letters of ADS, the everyday short form of advertisements
just = only recently, as in 'just arrived'

annotation.surface: Some advertising changes that have just been brought in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changes in advertisements' reads as one phrase; 'in' is surface only.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to adjust something is to change it slightly.

entries.clue: Old car of a certain hue with lots of indentations? (8)

blocks.note: a crate is a decrepit old car

annotation.surface: A battered old red banger covered in dents.
annotation.walkthrough: The dents fit the old car so well that the definition seems part of the description. A banger is British slang for an old car.
annotation.definitionFit: Cratered ground is pitted with holes; the question mark admits dents are a stretch.

entries.clue: Keep control, receiving thanks (6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: to receive is to take something in, so REIN takes TA inside it

annotation.surface: Advice to stay in charge while accepting gratitude.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep control' reads as one phrase, but 'Keep' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to retain something is to keep possession of it rather than give it up.

entries.clue: Some bunting always on display in Irish county (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used
indicatorNotes.on display: the answer is on show within the words

annotation.surface: Flags and bunting are a permanent feature of an Irish county.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Galway is a county on the west coast of Ireland, a definition by example.

entries.clue: Author supporting ecological reform, from what we hear (6)

indicatorNotes.from what we hear: what we hear is the sound of the words, so the answer is spelt differently from what is described

blocks.note: a greeny is an environmentalist; said aloud it gives the surname of the novelist Graham

annotation.surface: A writer rumoured to back environmental causes.
annotation.walkthrough: GREENY sounds like GREENE, as in Graham Greene. The definition is just 'Author'; the rest describes a supporter of green politics.
annotation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock, so a definition by example.

entries.clue: Depot others use, otherwise containing nothing (10)

indicatorNotes.otherwise: the letters are put otherwise, in a new order

annotation.surface: A warehouse that other people use, currently standing empty.
annotation.walkthrough: The O for nothing goes in among the rearranged letters of OTHERS USE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a depot is a place where goods are kept, which is exactly a house for storing them.

entries.clue: See 10
Super vehicle blocking road – feature of Newmarket event? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.blocking: a car blocking a road sits across it, so ACE CAR sits inside RD

annotation.surface: A fancy car stuck across the road on the way to the races.
annotation.walkthrough: Newmarket is an English town that is the home of horse racing. The answer continues at 2 down.
annotation.definitionFit: A race card is the printed programme listing the runners at a horse-racing meeting such as Newmarket's.

entries.clue: Enthusiast hugging one by church, fellow anticipating ceremony there? (6)

indicatorNotes.hugging: a hug wraps arms around someone, so FAN wraps around I

annotation.surface: An eager man waiting by the church for his wedding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to the church: the ceremony he anticipates is his wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man engaged to be married, awaiting the wedding.

entries.clue: Number coming to a place like Oxford must show perseverance (8)

annotation.surface: Getting into Oxford takes perseverance.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at Oxford University admissions, but Oxford only stands for a city.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tenacity is the quality of holding on and not giving up, which is perseverance.
